title: Samantha Ruth Prabhu Is Pregnant. The South's Most Watched Comeback Just Got Its Most Personal Chapter.
excerpt: Six months after a quiet temple wedding to Raj Nidimoru, the actress is expecting her first child. She hasn't said a word — but a baby bump she chose not to hide, and a director who couldn't keep the secret, said it for her.
body:
She walked back onto a stage in a white T-shirt, and the whole South leaned in. The occasion was the success bash for Maa Inti Bangaaram, the film that marked Samantha Ruth Prabhu's return to the big screen after a brutal, public battle with myositis. The fans came to celebrate the comeback. They left talking about something else entirely.

There was a softness to her silhouette that the cameras caught and the internet refused to drop. Within hours, the clips were everywhere, the speculation deafening. And then, the way these things always do in the South Indian film industry, the confirmation arrived not from the woman at the centre of it, but from someone who simply couldn't help themselves.

Samantha Ruth Prabhu is pregnant. She is expecting her first child with filmmaker Raj Nidimoru, the man she married in December 2025 after years of quiet companionship.

!Maa Inti Bangaaram — Photo: Wikimedia Commons

"She was aware of the bump, aware of the cameras, and made a conscious choice to appear anyway, before any announcement, on her own terms."
https://x.com/ZoomTV/status/2068321877190406625
"Her pregnancy comes at a beautiful time, as our film Maa Inti Bangaaram has become a success." — BV Nandini Reddy, director of Maa Inti Bangaaram

That single line, dropped to Cinema Express by the film's director, did what days of viral video could not. It turned rumour into record. Reddy, speaking with the warmth of someone who clearly adores her leading lady, also let slip the most telling detail of all: Samantha knew exactly what she was doing when she stepped out for that celebration. She was aware of the bump, aware of the cameras, and made a conscious choice to appear anyway, before any announcement, on her own terms. That is not a woman caught out. That is a woman who decided the moment belonged to her film first.

!South Indian — Photo: Wikimedia Commons

https://www.instagram.com/p/DZy8ddhhkSc/

It is a deeply Samantha move. For an actress whose private life has been picked apart in public more than almost anyone of her generation — the headlines after her 2021 separation were merciless, the health scare even more so — there is something quietly defiant about letting the world figure it out rather than performing the reveal. No staged photoshoot. No carefully captioned Instagram grid. Just a woman at a party for the film that gave her career back, glowing, and letting people draw their own conclusions.

The romance with Nidimoru has always run on this same low frequency. The two grew close on the set of The Family Man, the Amazon Prime spy series in which Samantha's turn as the chilling Raji rewired what audiences thought she was capable of. Nidimoru, one half of the Raj & DK directing duo behind that show and Citadel: Honey Bunny, was the creative partner who kept casting her against type. Somewhere between the action choreography and the edit suites, the working relationship became something more. They never confirmed it until they were ready, and when they were, they did it the most Samantha way possible — an intimate ceremony at Sadhguru's Isha Yoga Centre in Coimbatore, at the Linga Bhairavi Temple, with only the closest of friends and family in the room. No drone shots. No magazine cover. A temple, a small circle, and done.

For the diaspora that has followed her from Ye Maaya Chesave to the global reach of The Family Man, this lands differently. Samantha has become one of the rare South Indian stars whose name travels — streamed in living rooms from New Jersey to Surrey, claimed equally by Telugu households and the wider Indian audience that found her through OTT. Her health battle was followed anxiously across that diaspora; her comeback was cheered just as loudly. To see her step into motherhood now, on the back of a hit, feels less like gossip and more like a chapter the audience has earned alongside her.

There is also the small matter of timing and craft. Samantha and Nidimoru are not slowing down — both have a slate that keeps them in the OTT conversation, and the industry's worst-kept secret is that the couple work better together than most. A child does not pause a partnership built on collaboration; if anything, it deepens the mythology.

For now, the woman herself stays silent, which is precisely the point. Maa Inti Bangaaram is streaming and screening across markets where the diaspora can find it, and the success that Reddy was really there to celebrate keeps climbing. The baby news will be confirmed in Samantha's own time, in Samantha's own words, if she chooses to speak at all. Until then, she has done what she does best — walked into the spotlight on her terms, and let everyone else do the talking.
